rationale: The description concretely specifies accessibility functions—speech and Braille output and navigation/access to applications. It does not describe learned or AI-based speech generation; these stated screen-reader functions support a conventional description-based negative.
evidence_spans: JAWS provides speech and Braille output for the most popular computer applications on your PC.
You will be able to navigate the Internet, write a document, read an email and create presentations
conflict_response: The stated speech output does not by itself establish AI dependence, and I do not assume that speech synthesis is always conventional or always AI. Since the text gives clear accessibility functionality but no AI signal or unexplained AI-dependent operation, the negative is supported under the description-only rubric.
